Notes: Cursor LOGIC proven deterministically (5/5 self-test, re-validated by verify-local-gates): pointer + keyboard map to an in-bounds sample, Home/End jump to run start/end, a left-to-right drag updates the selected time continuously, and no operation selects outside the run window. The WEBVIEW render surface is wired into the extension: the openViewer command builds a strict-CSP nonce-scoped webview that renders the metric time-series as an SVG with a draggable vertical time cursor, and media/viewer.js delegates ALL cursor math to the shipped viewerCursor core (imported VERBATIM -- no duplicated snap logic); the .vsix bundles media/viewer.js + media/viewerCursor.mjs, the activation test asserts the CSP-safe HTML, and verify-local-gates #25 statically gates the surface. The render itself is now PROVEN EXECUTED: test/viewer-render.mjs loads media/viewer.js in a real DOM (jsdom) and asserts it renders the metric SVG (polyline + cursor line + selected dot) and that pointer drag + Left/Right + Home/End move the cursor over the run window (a right-edge drag snaps to the last sample and moves the cursor line; a ~42% drag snaps to the interior t=300 sample), executing the actual browser presentation code with the proven viewerCursor core doing the snap. The interactive render inside a real VS Code extension-host webview over the real mprr short-packet timingTicks64 axis is the remaining maintainer step.
